title: Aligned Delegates are forbidden from voting for an emergency spell until they have personally confirmed three preconditions
content:
A.1.10.5.2.3.3 states that ADs "are strictly prohibited from voting to use a Standby Spell unless they have first confirmed all of the following requirements": receipt of the Core Facilitator's official emergency notification via the Emergency Contact Mechanism; receipt of the Core Facilitator's announced decision in the Emergency Response Signal Group; and Core GovOps' authenticity validation, in writing, from the named Authorized Representatives. A.1.10.5.3.2.3 imposes the same triple check before voting for an Emergency Drop Spell or granting authority to Protego.

This is the mitigation for the attack surface A.1.10.5.2.1 admits Standby Spells create. A pre-approved, reusable, delay-bypassing spell is dangerous precisely because voting for it is cheap and routine — so the Atlas makes each delegate an independent checkpoint rather than a rubber stamp, and requires each of the three signals to arrive through a *different* channel controlled by a *different* party.

The rule also constrains what ADs may do once satisfied: they must "either (1) promptly vote to approve the Standby Spell, or (2) communicate any concerns to the Core Facilitator and collaborate with the latter for a speedy resolution." Silence is not an option. Abstention by inaction would let a delegate stall an emergency response without ever stating a reason, so the Atlas forces either a vote or an articulated objection.
description: ADs must confirm the official incident notification, the Core Facilitator's announced decision, and Core GovOps' written authenticity validation — converting the voter into a checkpoint.
